proposal_title: FlowExecutionPort Strict Discriminated Operations & Result Schema
domain_specific_rationale: From a Developer Experience, Code Generation, and AI Agent Handoff perspective, un-typed generic payload dictionaries (such as params: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: true } in v0.9.0 browser-command.schema.json) and un-schema'd return payloads represent severe ergonomic failure modes. When downstream engineering teams and autonomous coding agents attempt to implement adapters (R08_GOOGLE_FLOW_ADAPTER), worker executors (R09_BROWSER_WORKER), bridge proxies (R10_FLOWKIT_BRIDGE), or integration mock harnesses (R15_INTEGRATION_HARNESS), loose typing forces developers to guess parameter semantics and return envelopes, preventing automated TypeScript/Python interface generation (json-schema-to-typescript, pydantic-core). CP-003 solves this by introducing strict discriminated oneOf unions on command_type for all 10 operations (ENSURE_SESSION, OPEN_FLOW, CREATE_OR_SELECT_PROJECT, ATTACH_ASSETS, SET_GENERATION_OPTIONS, SUBMIT_PROMPT, READ_GENERATION_STATE, DOWNLOAD_OUTPUT, CAPTURE_DIAGNOSTIC, CANCEL) alongside a matching flow-execution-result.schema.json. This provides end-to-end static type safety, IDE autocompletion, compile-time validation, and deterministic mock fixture generation in local developer environments.
capability_impact: Directly reinforces CAP-03 (Google Flow Deep Integration), CAP-04 (Pluggable Provider Abstraction), CAP-16 (Hermetic Simulation & Testing), and CAP-18 (Dual-Track Replaceability) by guaranteeing compile-time and runtime interchangeability between Track A and Track B execution ports without developer ambiguity.
residual_risk: Introduction of future diagnostic properties could cause schema validation rejections in legacy workers if additionalProperties is set to false. Mitigated by versioned schema releases (v1.0.0 -> v1.1.0) and backward-compatible schema extension guidelines in API_COMPATIBILITY_POLICY.md.
